nodes.summary: With `p = q₁` and `q = 1 - q₁`, `V_A = 2pq (a + d (q - p)) ²`. An algebraic identity, valid for every real `q₁`; it is a variance for `0 ≤ q₁ ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Additive variance at a biallelic locus (Falconer & Mackay 1996, ch. 8)

nodes.summary: The additive genetic variance `V_A = 2 ∑ i p i α i ²`, the variance of the breeding value `α i + α j`.
nodes.title: Additive genetic variance

nodes.summary: The average effect of allele `i`, `α i = ∑ j p j G i j - μ`: the mean value of the genotypes carrying `i` (the other gene drawn from the population) minus the population mean. This is the average excess; under Hardy–Weinberg proportions it is Fisher's average effect, the coefficient of the least-squares additive fit (`domVar_le_sum_sq`).
nodes.title: Average effect of an allele

nodes.summary: Allele frequencies at a biallelic locus: `A₁` (`true`) has frequency `q₁` and `A₂` (`false`) has frequency `1 - q₁`.
nodes.title: Allele frequencies at a biallelic locus

nodes.summary: Genotypic values at a biallelic locus on Falconer's scale: `A₁A₁ ↦ a`, `A₁A₂ ↦ d`, `A₂A₂ ↦ -a` (the origin is the midpoint of the homozygotes).
nodes.title: Genotypic values at a biallelic locus on Falconer's scale

nodes.summary: `Cov(FS) = V_A / 2 + V_D / 4`.
nodes.title: Full sibs (Fisher 1918)

nodes.summary: The covariance of the genotypic values of full sibs: the sire `(i, j)` and the dam `(k, l)` are unrelated; the first offspring receives `cond b i j` and `cond e k l`, the second, independently, `cond b' i j` and `cond e' k l`.
nodes.title: Full-sib covariance of genotypic values

nodes.summary: `Cov(HS) = V_A / 4`.
nodes.title: Half sibs (Fisher 1918)

nodes.summary: The covariance of the genotypic values of half sibs: the common parent has genotype `(i, j)` and transmits `cond b i j` to one offspring and, independently, `cond b' i j` to the other; the second genes `k`, `l` come from two unrelated mates.
nodes.title: Half-sib covariance of genotypic values

nodes.summary: `Cov(P, O) = V_A / 2`.
nodes.title: Parent and offspring (Fisher 1918)

nodes.summary: The covariance of the genotypic values of a parent and its offspring: the parent has genotype `(i, j)` (frequency `p i p j`) and transmits `cond b i j` (each with probability `1/2`), and the offspring's other gene `k` comes from an unrelated mate (frequency `p k`).
nodes.title: Parent–offspring covariance of genotypic values

nodes.summary: The dominance deviation `δ i j = G i j - μ - α i - α j`.
nodes.title: Dominance deviation of a genotype

nodes.summary: `V_D = (2pqd) ²`, for every real `q₁`.
nodes.title: Dominance variance at a biallelic locus (Falconer & Mackay 1996, ch. 8)

nodes.summary: Among all fits `c + a i + a j` of the genotypic value by a function additive over the two genes, the additive fitted genotypic value `μ + α i + α j` minimizes the weighted squared error `∑ p i p j (G i j - c - a i - a j) ²`; its error is `V_D`.
nodes.title: Least squares (Fisher 1918)

nodes.summary: The dominance variance `V_D = ∑ i ∑ j p i p j δ i j ²`.
nodes.title: Dominance variance

nodes.summary: `V_G = V_A + V_D`.
nodes.title: Fisher's variance decomposition

nodes.summary: The genetic variance `V_G = ∑ i ∑ j p i p j (G i j - μ) ²`.
nodes.title: Genetic variance under Hardy–Weinberg proportions

nodes.summary: The decomposition `G i j = μ + α i + α j + δ i j` (an identity by definition of `δ`).
nodes.title: Decomposition of the genotypic value

nodes.summary: The mean genotypic value `μ = ∑ i ∑ j p i p j G i j` under Hardy–Weinberg proportions.
nodes.title: Mean genotypic value under Hardy–Weinberg proportions

nodes.summary: The average effects have mean zero: `∑ i p i α i = 0`.
nodes.title: Average effects have mean zero

nodes.summary: Orthogonality of the dominance deviations for a symmetric genotypic value: `∑ i p i δ i j = 0` for every `j`.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of dominance deviations in the first allele

nodes.summary: Orthogonality of the dominance deviations: `∑ j p j δ i j = 0` for every `i`.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of dominance deviations in the second allele

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
